Dear Bonnie,
  Here is a solution.  I found it at http://stackoverflow.com/questions/4765053/apply-a-list-of-n-functions-to-each-row-of-a-dataframe .  I changed it some and gave 3 versions:  1) doing it for a plain matrix of values, 2) doing it for a data frame of just numbers, and 3) doing it for a data frame of mixed values, strings and numbers.
In 3), R reduces everything to the lowest mode - string.
  I hope this helps.
      Ken Straus


 m
     [,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,]    1    3    5
[2,]    2    4    6
>
> fcns<-list(fcn1=function(x) x^2, fcn2=function(x) x^3, fcn3=function(x) 2*x^3)
> fcns
$fcn1
function (x)
x^2

$fcn2
function (x)
x^3

$fcn3
function (x)
2 * x^3

> mapply(do.call, fcns, apply(m,2,list))
     fcn1 fcn2 fcn3
[1,]    1   27  250
[2,]    4   64  432
>

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

> frm0<-data.frame(x1=c(1,2,3), x2=c(1.1,1.2,1.3), x3=c(4,5,6))
> frm0
  x1  x2 x3
1  1 1.1  4
2  2 1.2  5
3  3 1.3  6
>
>
> fcns0<-list(fcn1=function(x) x^2, fcn2=function(x) x^3, fcn3=function(x) 2*x^3)
> fcns0
$fcn1
function (x)
x^2

$fcn2
function (x)
x^3

$fcn3
function (x)
2 * x^3

>
> mapply(do.call, fcns0, lapply(frm0,list))
     fcn1  fcn2 fcn3
[1,]    1 1.331  128
[2,]    4 1.728  250
[3,]    9 2.197  432
>
>
>
> xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Error: object 'xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx' not found
>
>
> fcns<-list(fcn1=function(x) x^2, fcn2=function(x) paste(x,"0"), fcn3=function(x) x^3)
> fcns
$fcn1
function (x)
x^2

$fcn2
function (x)
paste(x, "0")

$fcn3
function (x)
x^3

> frm<-data.frame(x1=c(1,2,3), x2=c("abc", "xyz", "rst"), x3=c(4,5,6))
> frm
  x1  x2 x3
1  1 abc  4
2  2 xyz  5
3  3 rst  6
>
>
> mapply(do.call, fcns, lapply(frm,list))
     fcn1 fcn2    fcn3
[1,] "1"  "abc 0" "64"
[2,] "4"  "xyz 0" "125"
[3,] "9"  "rst 0" "216"
>
>
>

  • applying a different function to each column of a data frame [1 Update]
 applying a different function to each column of a data frame
    Bonnie Dixon <bmd...@ucdavis.edu> Aug 08 10:28PM -0700  

    Hi D-RUG folks.
     
    Does anyone know of a function for the following purpose? I would like to
    apply a list of functions to the columns of my data frame so that the first
    function in the list would be applied to the first column, the second
    function would be applied to the second column, the third function would be
    applied to the third column, etc. Is there a way to do this without using
    a loop?
     
    Bonnie

I think the mapply is a really good idea, but my wife points out that (in my example at least) the do.call isn't necessary.  I've appended her version.

-- Mike

myFns <- list(odds=sum, evens=mean)
myDF <- data.frame(
    cbind(
      dds=c(1, 3, 5, 7),
      evens=c(2, 4, 6, 8)
    )
  )

myDF

mapply(function(fn, column) {
      fn(column)
  }, myFns, myDF)

Wow!  Many thanks to Mike and Ken for the great ideas in response to my question.  I also learned (after much searching) that both ddply (from the plyr package) and the package, data.table have methods for doing this.  So, we have come up with four different ways to solve this problem.  I am attaching a script in which each of the methods is demonstrated on the example that Mike provided.  I agree that the approach Mike just showed with mapply seems like the winner for being most simple and straightforward.

Bonnie
